title: Comparison family split: 16 lanes over a tolerant arm and an exact-match control arm
status_plain: BUG-FUNC-004 is a two-arm experiment, and the arms disagree by design. Nine surfaces (the six comparison operators, SWITCH, COUNTIF, SUMIF) were routed through a shared helper that independently truncates each operand to 15 significant decimal digits and then compares the truncated doubles exactly. Three surfaces (MATCH, XMATCH, DELTA) were deliberately left OUT of that helper and kept on raw IEEE equality; they are the experiment's exact-match control group, and the source says so four separate times. The sign-off scored 16 hand-picked lanes spanning BOTH arms against live Excel 16.0 build 20026 and reports "16/16 typed bit matches; 0 mismatches". That is one group total over lanes, not a pass rate for any surface: no surface here has an individual figure, and the source's own enumeration of the lanes counts to 17 (14 tolerant + 3 contrast), not 16, so the 16 cannot be decomposed onto surfaces from the text. The helper is not an epsilon tolerance: two values arbitrarily close together but astride a truncation-bucket boundary compare UNEQUAL, and two values far apart inside one bucket compare EQUAL. The source's own word for it is "truncation-style", never "tolerant" as a description of the arithmetic. The lanes that were signed off include the arithmetic-generated boundary pair the helper was corrected against after its first model diverged, so the scored corpus is the repair's own fitting set.

substrate: crates/oxfunc_core/src/functions/excel_numeric_compare.rs :: compare_excel_numbers / excel_numbers_equal — truncate each operand to 15 significant decimal digits toward zero, then compare exactly. Exhaustive caller set in crates/: operator_compare_concat_family.rs, criteria_family.rs, database_family.rs, misc_switch_info_family.rs. match_fn.rs, xmatch.rs and delta_fn.rs do not import it.
ruled_out: Round-to-nearest at 15 significant digits: the first helper model rounded rather than truncated and still diverged from Excel on the arithmetic-generated boundary pair ((123456789012345*10)+5)/1E25 versus ((123456789012345*10)+4)/1E25 (docs/bugs/streams/BUG-FUNC-004_numeric_comparison_tolerance_family_split.md:116-122).
open_question: The lanes enumerated at docs/bugs/streams/BUG-FUNC-004_numeric_comparison_tolerance_family_split.md:15-21 count to 17 (14 tolerant + 3 contrast) while the source reports 16/16. The source does not resolve the discrepancy and this record does not compose a decomposition.
reader_warning: Do not read this as "MATCH, XMATCH and DELTA compare tolerantly". They do the opposite: they use raw IEEE equality and exist in this record as the control arm. Do not read the 16/16 as any surface's pass rate; it is a total over 16 hand-picked lanes at build 20026, not over the surfaces themselves. And note that the axis here is structural-admission by the Handbook's own axis definition, so a page rendering "no numeric comparison record" for these six surfaces means "no bit-exactness comparison" - not "no numeric evidence"; this record is entirely about comparing numbers.
